# Instrucciones de cada nodo del grafo (P08)

## plan (agente)
You are the planning node of a graph. Read feature.md and, if present, state.md and any verdict files that say LAYER: requirements. Write spec.md: the scope, numbered acceptance criteria that can be checked in the running app, and anything that is out of scope. Do not write application code. Commit spec.md.

## implement (agente)
You are the implementation node of a graph. Read spec.md, AGENTS.md and state.md. If state.md lists feedback from verification or from a human, fix every point. Implement the feature, run npm run check, npm test, bash scripts/check-architecture.sh and bash scripts/smoke-bridge.sh, and commit. Do not edit spec.md, state.md or verdict files.

## verify-functional (agente, en su propio worktree)
You are the functional verification node of a graph. You do not modify application code. Build and launch the app (env -u NODE_OPTIONS npx electron . --remote-debugging-port=<port> --user-data-dir=<temp dir>), import data/sample-documents/, ask questions, and check every acceptance criterion in spec.md through window.knowledgeBase and the UI over Chrome DevTools (see scripts/check-bridge.mjs). Write verdict-functional.md. First line exactly VERDICT: PASS or VERDICT: FAIL. Second line exactly LAYER: none, LAYER: implementation (the code does not do what spec.md says) or LAYER: requirements (spec.md itself is wrong or incomplete for feature.md). Then numbered defects with evidence.

## verify-review (agente, en su propio worktree)
You are the code review node of a graph. You do not modify application code. Review the diff since the commit that added spec.md: correctness against spec.md and feature.md, layer boundaries in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, tests for the new behavior, dead code, and whether spec.md misread feature.md. Run npm run check, npm test and bash scripts/check-architecture.sh. Write verdict-review.md with the same first two lines (VERDICT and LAYER) and numbered findings with file and line.

# Feature: export the conversation as Markdown

`window.knowledgeBase.conversation.export()` returns a Markdown string with every question and answer in the conversation, in order, each answer followed by its citations (document title and excerpt). An empty conversation returns a Markdown document that says there are no questions yet. The question panel has a button with aria-label 'Export conversation' that saves that Markdown to a file chosen by the user.

# loop-state.md

Loop: maker-checker para búsqueda de documentos. Para con 2 PASS seguidos o 6 vueltas.

## Vuelta 1

### Maker (round 1)

**What changed**
- `DocumentService.searchDocuments(query)`: case-insensitive substring match on `title` or stored content (`content/<id>.txt`). Blank query (`''`, whitespace, `undefined`/`null`) returns `listDocuments()`. Non-blank query is trimmed. Literal text, not regex. Non-string query -> `TypeError`.
- New IPC channel `documents:search` (`IPC_CHANNELS.SEARCH_DOCUMENTS`) -> handler -> preload `documents.search(query)`; renderer type in `types.d.ts`.
- UI: `DocumentList` now always renders `<input type="search" aria-label="Search documents">`. `App` keeps `searchQuery`; on every change (and when the document set changes) it calls `documents.search`; a sequence counter makes only the latest response apply. Blank query shows `documents` directly (no IPC). No match -> "No documents match "<q>"." (role=status). Zero documents -> the existing "No documents imported yet." message (input still shown). Reset clears the query. Header "Documents (N)" still shows the total, not the filtered count.
- Docs: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (preload API, 15 channels, table row, DocumentList). `feature_list.json`: new `document-search`, state `active` (left for the Checker to decide).

**Files**: `src/services/document-service.ts`, `src/shared/types.ts`, `src/main/ipc-handlers.ts`, `src/preload/preload.ts`, `src/renderer/types.d.ts`, `src/renderer/App.tsx`, `src/renderer/components/DocumentList.tsx`, `tests/document-search.test.tsx` (new, 16 tests), `scripts/e2e/document-search.mjs` (new), `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `feature_list.json`, `session-handoff.md`, `claude-progress.md`.

**Verification (Maker, 2026-11-16)**
- `bash init.sh` (start) -> `init.sh OK` on the untouched baseline.
- `npm run check` -> no errors.
- `npm test` -> `Test Files 5 passed (5)`, `Tests 38 passed (38)` (was 22; +16 in document-search.test.tsx: title/content match, case, multiple matches, blank query, no match, literal `$5.00 (approx`, deleted docs excluded, restart, non-string rejected, preload channel, IPC handler, DocumentList input/filtered/no-match/empty).
- `bash scripts/check-architecture.sh` -> `PASS: All architecture boundary checks passed`.
- `bash scripts/smoke-bridge.sh` -> keys `documents,indexing,qa,feedback,app`, `PASS: the running app exposes window.knowledgeBase`.
- `env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm run build && node --experimental-websocket scripts/e2e/document-search.mjs` -> `all 10 checks passed` (real app, 3 sample docs: bridge title/content/empty/no-match; UI typing "ATTENDEES" keystroke-by-keystroke -> only meeting-summary; "Design-Notes" -> only design-notes; no match -> empty list + message; clearing -> all 3).
- Regression e2e: answer-feedback 7/7, reset-all-data 6/6, conversation-history 13/13.
- `bash init.sh` (end) -> `init.sh OK`.
- First e2e run failed on MY test expectation: I expected "design" to match only design-notes, but retrieval-plan's content contains "design"; the app was right. Changed the query to "Design-Notes" (title-only).

**Unsure about (please check)**
1. Trimming: `"  zebra "` searches for `zebra`. The spec says "contains query"; a literal reading would search with the spaces. Whitespace-only is treated as empty.
2. "Documents (N)" header shows the total, not the filtered count. Spec does not say.
3. Search is content-based via the main process, so each keystroke is one IPC call (no debounce). Fine for the sample size; not measured on large libraries.
4. Stale `content/<id>.txt` files of deleted docs are not deleted by `deleteDocument` (pre-existing), but search only scans listed docs, so they don't show up (unit test covers this).
5. The search input is not cleared when switching to a document view or on Refresh (only on Reset).
6. No UI import picker exists (pre-existing); e2e imports via `window.knowledgeBase.documents.import(path)`.

### Checker (round 1)

**Verdict: PASS**

**Defects:** none blocking.
**Observations (non-blocking):**
1. The query is trimmed: `search("attendees ")` -> `["meeting-summary"]`, but a literal "contains" check returns `[]`. `"   "` returns all docs.
2. The header count shows the total, not the filtered count.
3. A bridge import needs a Refresh before the list updates (this was already the case).

**What I ran:** `npm run check`, `npm test` (38/38), `check-architecture.sh` (PASS), `smoke-bridge.sh` (PASS), `npm run build`. The Maker's e2e scripts: document-search 10/10, answer-feedback 7/7, reset-all-data 6/6, conversation-history 13/13. My own `evaluation/checker-round1.mjs` (real CDP keystrokes, results checked against a brute-force oracle, plus ask/conversation/import regressions): 28/28 passed. Details are in `checker-verdict.md`.

## Vuelta 2

### Maker (round 2)

No Maker changes this round. The application code is unchanged since 402c7ee.

### Checker (round 2)

**Verdict: PASS** (second PASS in a row)

**Defects:** none.
**Observations (non-blocking):** the same as round 1: the query is trimmed, the header shows the total count, and a bridge import or delete needs a Refresh. Out of scope and pre-existing: asking "What are the meeting attendees?" cites retrieval-plan and design-notes, not meeting-summary. This is retrieval quality; the search change doesn't touch Q&A or retrieval code.

**What I ran:** `npm run check`, `npm test` (38/38), `check-architecture.sh` (PASS), `smoke-bridge.sh` (PASS), `npm run build`. Regression: document-search 10/10, answer-feedback 7/7, reset-all-data 6/6, conversation-history 13/13, checker-round1 28/28. New `evaluation/checker-round2.mjs` checked results against an oracle: 35/35 passed. It covered non-ASCII case-insensitivity, a match at the end of a ~120 KB file, title-only matches, rejection of bad input, rapid and concurrent keystrokes and stale-response races, paste, select-all-clear, delete while filtered, a real restart, Reset with a filter active, re-import after Reset, and asking with a filter active. Details are in `checker-verdict.md`.

Under the loop rule (stop after 2 PASS in a row), the loop can stop here.
# Product Description -- Knowledge Base (Capstone)

## What Is This?

A desktop application for managing a personal knowledge base. Users import text and Markdown documents, the system indexes them into searchable chunks, and provides grounded question answering with citations. Users can view conversation history, provide feedback on answers, and reset the application to a clean state for testing.

## Core Features

### Document Management
- Import `.txt` and `.md` files through a file picker in the ImportPanel.
- File validation: existence check, 10 MB size limit.
- View document metadata: title, filename, size, import date, indexing status.
- View document chunks with metadata (character count, word count).
- Browse a list of all imported documents in a sidebar panel.
- Delete documents and their associated data (content file, original copy).

### Text Indexing
- Split documents into ~500-character chunks at paragraph boundaries.
- Store chunks with metadata (character count, word count).
- Track indexing status per document and overall.
- Support indexing individual documents or the full library.
- Documents automatically marked as "indexed" after chunking.
- Indexing status visible in sidebar and status bar.

### Grounded Q&A
- Ask natural language questions about the document library.
- Receive answers with citations pointing to specific document chunks.
- Confidence scores indicate answer reliability (0.85 with citations, 0.30 without).
- 8 mock answer patterns covering architecture, import, indexing, retrieval, meetings, logging, feedback, and clean state.
- Full Q&A history is persisted across sessions.
- Query latency typically under 500ms.

### Conversation History
- Chat-style display of all Q&A exchanges.
- User questions shown as purple bubbles (right-aligned).
- Assistant answers shown as dark bubbles (left-aligned).
- Expandable citations for each answer.
- Confidence indicator with color coding (green/yellow/red).
- Timestamps on each exchange.
- Clear history with confirmation dialog.

### Feedback Collection
- Thumbs up/down buttons on each Q&A response in conversation history.
- Thumbs up/down buttons on the latest response in document view.
- Feedback persists across sessions.
- Each feedback entry includes: ID, Q&A timestamp, question, rating, optional comment, submission time.

### Clean State Reset
- Reset button in application header.
- Confirmation dialog before reset.
- Clears all documents, chunks, Q&A history, and feedback.
- Application returns to initial empty state.
- Data directory is removed and recreated.

### Persistence
- All data persists across application restarts.
- Document list loads automatically on application startup.
- Data stored locally in the user's application data directory.
- Four data files: documents-meta.json, qa-history.json, feedback.json, index-meta.json.

### Status Bar
- Real-time display of index status (idle, indexing, ready, error).
- Color-coded status indicator.
- Document count.
- Indexed document count.
- Last activity timestamp.

## User Interface

```
+------------------+----------------------------------------+
| Header           | History | Reset | Refresh              |
+------------------+----------------------------------------+
| Document List    | Document Detail / Conversation History |
| (sidebar)        |   - Metadata display                   |
|                  |   - Show Chunks toggle                 |
| [+ Import]       |   - Index Document button              |
|                  |   - Delete button                      |
| doc1 (Indexed)   |                                        |
|   3.2 KB         | Q&A Response:                          |
| doc2 (Imported)  |   Answer text...                       |
|   1.8 KB         |   Citations: [expandable]              |
|                  |   Confidence: high                     |
|                  |   [+1] [-1] feedback                   |
+------------------+----------------------------------------+
| Ask a question...                              [Ask]       |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
| Status: Ready | Documents: 3 | Indexed: 3 | 12:34 PM     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
```

## Constraints

- Maximum supported file size: 10 MB.
- Supported formats: `.txt`, `.md`.
- Q&A uses mock patterns -- no LLM integration.
- All data is local; no network requests.
- Structured logging outputs to console (no file-based logging in this version).

## Performance Targets

- Import throughput: 10+ files per batch under 1 second.
- Indexing speed: 100+ chunks per second.
- Query latency: under 500ms per question.
- Citation accuracy: top 2 chunks must be relevant.
# Architecture -- Knowledge Base Electron App (Capstone)

## System Overview

The Knowledge Base is an Electron desktop application built with TypeScript and React. It provides document import, text indexing with chunking, content viewing, grounded question answering with citations, feedback collection, conversation history, and runtime observability through structured logging.

This is the capstone project combining all features from the Learn Harness Engineering course.

## Layer Diagram

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
|                     Renderer (React)                       |
|  App.tsx -> DocumentList, DocumentDetail, ImportPanel,    |
|             QuestionPanel, ConversationHistory, StatusBar  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
         |  window.knowledgeBase.* (typed IPC bridge)
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
|                     Preload Script                         |
|  contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld ->                       |
|    documents, indexing, qa, feedback, app                  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
         |  ipcRenderer.invoke(IPC_CHANNELS.*)
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
|                     Main Process                           |
|  main.ts -> createWindow(), initializeServices()          |
|  ipc-handlers.ts -> registerIpcHandlers() (15 channels)   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
         |  Service method calls
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
|                     Services Layer                         |
|  DocumentService | IndexingService | QaService             |
|  PersistenceService (filesystem I/O)                       |
|  Logger (structured JSON output)                           |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
```

## Electron Layers

### Main Process (`src/main/`)

- **Window management**: Creates `BrowserWindow` instances with secure web preferences.
- **IPC registration**: Maps 15 IPC channel names to service methods via `registerIpcHandlers()`.
- **Service initialization**: Constructs all services with dependency injection.
- **Logging**: Logs application lifecycle events (ready, shutdown).

### Preload (`src/preload/`)

The preload script exposes a typed API via `contextBridge`:

```typescript
window.knowledgeBase = {
  documents: { list, import, get, delete, search },
  indexing:   { start, status, chunks },
  qa:         { ask, history, clearHistory },
  feedback:   { submit, list },
  app:        { reset },
}
```

### Renderer (`src/renderer/`)

React 18 application bundled by Vite:

- `App.tsx` -- Root layout; owns Q&A history + ratings; switches between the conversation and a selected document; Reset all data button (`ResetDataButton`, in-page confirmation).
- `DocumentList` -- Sidebar listing of imported documents with status and chunk counts, and a 'Search documents' input. App calls `documents.search(query)` as the user types (only the latest response is applied); a blank query shows all documents.
- `DocumentDetail` -- Shows metadata, chunks, indexing controls, and delete button.
- `ImportPanel` -- File input for importing .txt and .md documents.
- `QuestionPanel` -- Text input for asking questions.
- `ConversationHistory` -- Chat-style Q&A history with expandable citations, confidence indicators, feedback buttons, and clear history.
- `StatusBar` -- Shows index status, document count, indexed count, and last activity.

### Services (`src/services/`)

- `Logger` -- Structured JSON logging with DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR levels, service tags, and data payloads.
- `PersistenceService` -- Low-level JSON/text file I/O with atomic writes and reset capability.
- `DocumentService` -- Document CRUD with validation, content storage, and cleanup.
- `IndexingService` -- Paragraph-aware chunking (~500 chars), index management, and metrics.
- `QaService` -- Mock Q&A with keyword retrieval, citations, feedback, and duration tracking.

## Full Data Flow

### Document Import Flow

```
1. User selects file via ImportPanel
2. App.tsx calls window.knowledgeBase.documents.import(filePath)
3. Preload bridge invokes ipcRenderer.invoke('documents:import', filePath)
4. ipc-handlers.ts delegates to DocumentService.importDocument(filePath)
5. DocumentService:
   a. Validates file exists and is under 10MB
   b. Reads file content and stats
   c. Creates Document metadata object with UUID
   d. Copies file to documents directory via PersistenceService
   e. Stores extracted text content via PersistenceService
   f. Appends to documents-meta.json
   g. Logs structured event with documentId, filename, size
6. Result flows back through IPC
7. App.tsx calls refreshDocuments() to update the list
```

### Q&A Flow with Observability

```
1. User types question in QuestionPanel
2. App.tsx calls window.knowledgeBase.qa.ask(question)
3. QaService.ask():
   a. Logs question with length
   b. Simulates processing delay (100-500ms)
   c. Gets all chunks from IndexingService
   d. Tokenizes question into keywords (length > 2)
   e. Scores each chunk by keyword overlap count
   f. Selects top 2 chunks as citations
   g. Generates answer from mock patterns or fallback
   h. Creates QAResponse with confidence score
   i. Saves to qa-history.json
   j. Logs answer with confidence, citationCount, durationMs
4. Result flows to renderer
5. App.tsx displays answer with citations and feedback buttons
```

### Feedback Flow

```
1. User clicks 'Mark answer helpful' / 'Mark answer not helpful' on an answer (AnswerFeedback)
2. Renderer calls window.knowledgeBase.feedback.submit(answerId, 'up' | 'down')  (answerId = QAResponse.id)
3. FeedbackService.submit():
   a. Rejects a rating other than 'up'/'down' and answer ids not in qa-history.json
   b. Stores {answerId, rating, timestamp} in feedback.json, replacing an earlier rating of the same answer
   c. Logs structured event
4. window.knowledgeBase.feedback.list() returns [{answerId, rating, timestamp}]
4. Feedback persists across sessions
```

### Clean State Reset Flow

```
1. User clicks the header button with aria-label 'Reset all data'
2. In-page confirmation dialog (role=alertdialog) appears; Cancel deletes nothing
3. ResetDataButton calls window.knowledgeBase.app.reset()  (IPC app:reset)
4. PersistenceService.resetAll():
   a. Removes entire data directory (rmSync recursive)
   b. Recreates directory structure
   c. Logs reset event
5. App.tsx clears all React state
6. refreshDocuments() reloads empty state
```

## IPC Channels (15 total)

| Channel | Direction | Handler | Purpose |
|---------|-----------|---------|---------|
| `documents:list` | R -> M | DocumentService.listDocuments | List all documents |
| `documents:import` | R -> M | DocumentService.importDocument | Import a file |
| `documents:get` | R -> M | DocumentService.getDocument | Get document by ID |
| `documents:delete` | R -> M | DocumentService.deleteDocument | Delete document |
| `documents:search` | R -> M | DocumentService.searchDocuments | Documents whose title or content contains the query (case-insensitive, trimmed; blank = all) |
| `indexing:start` | R -> M | IndexingService.startIndexing | Start indexing |
| `indexing:status` | R -> M | IndexingService.getStatus | Get indexing status |
| `indexing:chunks` | R -> M | IndexingService.getChunksForDocument | Get chunks |
| `qa:ask` | R -> M | QaService.ask | Ask a question |
| `qa:history` | R -> M | QaService.getHistory | Get Q&A history |
| `qa:clear-history` | R -> M | QaService.clearHistory | Clear history |
| `feedback:submit` | R -> M | FeedbackService.submit | Submit feedback |
| `feedback:list` | R -> M | FeedbackService.list | Get all feedback |
| `app:reset` | R -> M | PersistenceService.resetAll | Reset all data |
| `app:status` | R -> M | IndexingService.getStatus | Get app status |

## Data Storage

```
knowledge-base-data/
  documents-meta.json     # Document metadata array
  content/
    <doc-id>.txt          # Extracted text content per document
  documents/
    <filename>            # Original file copies
  chunks/
    <doc-id>.json         # Chunk array per document
  index/
    index-meta.json       # Mapping of document IDs to chunk IDs
  qa-history.json         # Q&A interaction log
  feedback.json           # Feedback entries
```

## Logging

All log entries follow this JSON structure:

```json
{
  "timestamp": "2026-03-30T12:00:00.000Z",
  "level": "INFO",
  "service": "document-service",
  "message": "Document imported successfully",
  "data": {
    "documentId": "abc-123",
    "filename": "design-notes.md",
    "sizeBytes": 2048,
    "contentLength": 1980,
    "totalDocuments": 3
  }
}
```

Log levels:
- **DEBUG**: Routine data access (listing, reading files, chunk retrieval)
- **INFO**: Significant events (import, indexing, Q&A, feedback, reset)
- **WARN**: Missing but non-critical data (skipped documents, content not found)
- **ERROR**: Failures (file not found, parse errors)

## Preload build

Electron runs the preload sandboxed, so it may only `require('electron')`. `npm run build` bundles
`src/preload/preload.ts` (including `src/shared/types`) into one file with `scripts/build-preload.js`
(esbuild). Do not disable the sandbox; `scripts/check-architecture.sh` fails if the bundle has local requires.

# Product Description -- Knowledge Base (Capstone)

## What Is This?

A desktop application for managing a personal knowledge base. Users import text and Markdown documents, the system indexes them into searchable chunks, and provides grounded question answering with citations. Users can view conversation history, provide feedback on answers, and reset the application to a clean state for testing.

## Core Features

### Document Management
- Import `.txt` and `.md` files through a file picker in the ImportPanel.
- File validation: existence check, 10 MB size limit.
- View document metadata: title, filename, size, import date, indexing status.
- View document chunks with metadata (character count, word count).
- Browse a list of all imported documents in a sidebar panel.
- Delete documents and their associated data (content file, original copy).

### Text Indexing
- Split documents into ~500-character chunks at paragraph boundaries.
- Store chunks with metadata (character count, word count).
- Track indexing status per document and overall.
- Support indexing individual documents or the full library.
- Documents automatically marked as "indexed" after chunking.
- Indexing status visible in sidebar and status bar.

### Grounded Q&A
- Ask natural language questions about the document library.
- Receive answers with citations pointing to specific document chunks.
- Confidence scores indicate answer reliability (0.85 with citations, 0.30 without).
- 8 mock answer patterns covering architecture, import, indexing, retrieval, meetings, logging, feedback, and clean state.
- Full Q&A history is persisted across sessions.
- Query latency typically under 500ms.

### Conversation History
- Chat-style display of all Q&A exchanges.
- User questions shown as purple bubbles (right-aligned).
- Assistant answers shown as dark bubbles (left-aligned).
- Expandable citations for each answer.
- Confidence indicator with color coding (green/yellow/red).
- Timestamps on each exchange.
- Clear history with confirmation dialog.

### Feedback Collection
- Thumbs up/down buttons on each Q&A response in conversation history.
- Thumbs up/down buttons on the latest response in document view.
- Feedback persists across sessions.
- Each feedback entry includes: ID, Q&A timestamp, question, rating, optional comment, submission time.

### Clean State Reset
- Reset button in application header.
- Confirmation dialog before reset.
- Clears all documents, chunks, Q&A history, and feedback.
- Application returns to initial empty state.
- Data directory is removed and recreated.

### Persistence
- All data persists across application restarts.
- Document list loads automatically on application startup.
- Data stored locally in the user's application data directory.
- Four data files: documents-meta.json, qa-history.json, feedback.json, index-meta.json.

### Status Bar
- Real-time display of index status (idle, indexing, ready, error).
- Color-coded status indicator.
- Document count.
- Indexed document count.
- Last activity timestamp.

## User Interface

```
+------------------+----------------------------------------+
| Header           | History | Reset | Refresh              |
+------------------+----------------------------------------+
| Document List    | Document Detail / Conversation History |
| (sidebar)        |   - Metadata display                   |
|                  |   - Show Chunks toggle                 |
| [+ Import]       |   - Index Document button              |
|                  |   - Delete button                      |
| doc1 (Indexed)   |                                        |
|   3.2 KB         | Q&A Response:                          |
| doc2 (Imported)  |   Answer text...                       |
|   1.8 KB         |   Citations: [expandable]              |
|                  |   Confidence: high                     |
|                  |   [+1] [-1] feedback                   |
+------------------+----------------------------------------+
| Ask a question...                              [Ask]       |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
| Status: Ready | Documents: 3 | Indexed: 3 | 12:34 PM     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
```

## Constraints

- Maximum supported file size: 10 MB.
- Supported formats: `.txt`, `.md`.
- Q&A uses mock patterns -- no LLM integration.
- All data is local; no network requests.
- Structured logging outputs to console (no file-based logging in this version).

## Performance Targets

- Import throughput: 10+ files per batch under 1 second.
- Indexing speed: 100+ chunks per second.
- Query latency: under 500ms per question.
- Citation accuracy: top 2 chunks must be relevant.
# Architecture -- Knowledge Base Electron App (Capstone)

## System Overview

The Knowledge Base is an Electron desktop application built with TypeScript and React. It provides document import, text indexing with chunking, content viewing, grounded question answering with citations, feedback collection, conversation history, and runtime observability through structured logging.

This is the capstone project combining all features from the Learn Harness Engineering course.

## Layer Diagram

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
|                     Renderer (React)                       |
|  App.tsx -> DocumentList, DocumentDetail, ImportPanel,    |
|             QuestionPanel, ConversationHistory, StatusBar  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
         |  window.knowledgeBase.* (typed IPC bridge)
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
|                     Preload Script                         |
|  contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld ->                       |
|    documents, indexing, qa, feedback, app                  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
         |  ipcRenderer.invoke(IPC_CHANNELS.*)
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
|                     Main Process                           |
|  main.ts -> createWindow(), initializeServices()          |
|  ipc-handlers.ts -> registerIpcHandlers() (15 channels)   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
         |  Service method calls
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
|                     Services Layer                         |
|  DocumentService | IndexingService | QaService             |
|  PersistenceService (filesystem I/O)                       |
|  Logger (structured JSON output)                           |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
```

## Electron Layers

### Main Process (`src/main/`)

- **Window management**: Creates `BrowserWindow` instances with secure web preferences.
- **IPC registration**: Maps 15 IPC channel names to service methods via `registerIpcHandlers()`.
- **Service initialization**: Constructs all services with dependency injection.
- **Logging**: Logs application lifecycle events (ready, shutdown).

### Preload (`src/preload/`)

The preload script exposes a typed API via `contextBridge`:

```typescript
window.knowledgeBase = {
  documents: { list, import, get, delete, search },
  indexing:   { start, status, chunks },
  qa:         { ask, history, clearHistory },
  feedback:   { submit, list },
  app:        { reset },
}
```

### Renderer (`src/renderer/`)

React 18 application bundled by Vite:

- `App.tsx` -- Root layout; owns Q&A history + ratings; switches between the conversation and a selected document; Reset all data button (`ResetDataButton`, in-page confirmation).
- `DocumentList` -- Sidebar listing of imported documents with status and chunk counts, and a 'Search documents' input. App calls `documents.search(query)` as the user types (only the latest response is applied); a blank query shows all documents.
- `DocumentDetail` -- Shows metadata, chunks, indexing controls, and delete button.
- `ImportPanel` -- File input for importing .txt and .md documents.
- `QuestionPanel` -- Text input for asking questions.
- `ConversationHistory` -- Chat-style Q&A history with expandable citations, confidence indicators, feedback buttons, and clear history.
- `StatusBar` -- Shows index status, document count, indexed count, and last activity.

### Services (`src/services/`)

- `Logger` -- Structured JSON logging with DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR levels, service tags, and data payloads.
- `PersistenceService` -- Low-level JSON/text file I/O with atomic writes and reset capability.
- `DocumentService` -- Document CRUD with validation, content storage, and cleanup.
- `IndexingService` -- Paragraph-aware chunking (~500 chars), index management, and metrics.
- `QaService` -- Mock Q&A with keyword retrieval, citations, feedback, and duration tracking.

## Full Data Flow

### Document Import Flow

```
1. User selects file via ImportPanel
2. App.tsx calls window.knowledgeBase.documents.import(filePath)
3. Preload bridge invokes ipcRenderer.invoke('documents:import', filePath)
4. ipc-handlers.ts delegates to DocumentService.importDocument(filePath)
5. DocumentService:
   a. Validates file exists and is under 10MB
   b. Reads file content and stats
   c. Creates Document metadata object with UUID
   d. Copies file to documents directory via PersistenceService
   e. Stores extracted text content via PersistenceService
   f. Appends to documents-meta.json
   g. Logs structured event with documentId, filename, size
6. Result flows back through IPC
7. App.tsx calls refreshDocuments() to update the list
```

### Q&A Flow with Observability

```
1. User types question in QuestionPanel
2. App.tsx calls window.knowledgeBase.qa.ask(question)
3. QaService.ask():
   a. Logs question with length
   b. Simulates processing delay (100-500ms)
   c. Gets all chunks from IndexingService
   d. Tokenizes question into keywords (length > 2)
   e. Scores each chunk by keyword overlap count
   f. Selects top 2 chunks as citations
   g. Generates answer from mock patterns or fallback
   h. Creates QAResponse with confidence score
   i. Saves to qa-history.json
   j. Logs answer with confidence, citationCount, durationMs
4. Result flows to renderer
5. App.tsx displays answer with citations and feedback buttons
```

### Feedback Flow

```
1. User clicks 'Mark answer helpful' / 'Mark answer not helpful' on an answer (AnswerFeedback)
2. Renderer calls window.knowledgeBase.feedback.submit(answerId, 'up' | 'down')  (answerId = QAResponse.id)
3. FeedbackService.submit():
   a. Rejects a rating other than 'up'/'down' and answer ids not in qa-history.json
   b. Stores {answerId, rating, timestamp} in feedback.json, replacing an earlier rating of the same answer
   c. Logs structured event
4. window.knowledgeBase.feedback.list() returns [{answerId, rating, timestamp}]
4. Feedback persists across sessions
```

### Clean State Reset Flow

```
1. User clicks the header button with aria-label 'Reset all data'
2. In-page confirmation dialog (role=alertdialog) appears; Cancel deletes nothing
3. ResetDataButton calls window.knowledgeBase.app.reset()  (IPC app:reset)
4. PersistenceService.resetAll():
   a. Removes entire data directory (rmSync recursive)
   b. Recreates directory structure
   c. Logs reset event
5. App.tsx clears all React state
6. refreshDocuments() reloads empty state
```

## IPC Channels (15 total)

| Channel | Direction | Handler | Purpose |
|---------|-----------|---------|---------|
| `documents:list` | R -> M | DocumentService.listDocuments | List all documents |
| `documents:import` | R -> M | DocumentService.importDocument | Import a file |
| `documents:get` | R -> M | DocumentService.getDocument | Get document by ID |
| `documents:delete` | R -> M | DocumentService.deleteDocument | Delete document |
| `documents:search` | R -> M | DocumentService.searchDocuments | Documents whose title or content contains the query (case-insensitive, trimmed; blank = all) |
| `indexing:start` | R -> M | IndexingService.startIndexing | Start indexing |
| `indexing:status` | R -> M | IndexingService.getStatus | Get indexing status |
| `indexing:chunks` | R -> M | IndexingService.getChunksForDocument | Get chunks |
| `qa:ask` | R -> M | QaService.ask | Ask a question |
| `qa:history` | R -> M | QaService.getHistory | Get Q&A history |
| `qa:clear-history` | R -> M | QaService.clearHistory | Clear history |
| `feedback:submit` | R -> M | FeedbackService.submit | Submit feedback |
| `feedback:list` | R -> M | FeedbackService.list | Get all feedback |
| `app:reset` | R -> M | PersistenceService.resetAll | Reset all data |
| `app:status` | R -> M | IndexingService.getStatus | Get app status |

## Data Storage

```
knowledge-base-data/
  documents-meta.json     # Document metadata array
  content/
    <doc-id>.txt          # Extracted text content per document
  documents/
    <filename>            # Original file copies
  chunks/
    <doc-id>.json         # Chunk array per document
  index/
    index-meta.json       # Mapping of document IDs to chunk IDs
  qa-history.json         # Q&A interaction log
  feedback.json           # Feedback entries
```

## Logging

All log entries follow this JSON structure:

```json
{
  "timestamp": "2026-03-30T12:00:00.000Z",
  "level": "INFO",
  "service": "document-service",
  "message": "Document imported successfully",
  "data": {
    "documentId": "abc-123",
    "filename": "design-notes.md",
    "sizeBytes": 2048,
    "contentLength": 1980,
    "totalDocuments": 3
  }
}
```

Log levels:
- **DEBUG**: Routine data access (listing, reading files, chunk retrieval)
- **INFO**: Significant events (import, indexing, Q&A, feedback, reset)
- **WARN**: Missing but non-critical data (skipped documents, content not found)
- **ERROR**: Failures (file not found, parse errors)

## Preload build

Electron runs the preload sandboxed, so it may only `require('electron')`. `npm run build` bundles
`src/preload/preload.ts` (including `src/shared/types`) into one file with `scripts/build-preload.js`
(esbuild). Do not disable the sandbox; `scripts/check-architecture.sh` fails if the bundle has local requires.

# spec.md: export the conversation as Markdown

Source: `feature.md`. Round 1, no earlier verdicts.

## Scope

"The conversation" is the persisted Q&A history: what `window.knowledgeBase.qa.history()` returns, in that order
(oldest first, the same order the conversation view shows). Two parts are added:

1. **Bridge:** `window.knowledgeBase.conversation.export()` returns `Promise<string>`, a Markdown document built
   from the current history. It reads the history every time it runs and changes no data.
2. **UI:** the question panel gets a button with `aria-label="Export conversation"`. Clicking it gets the Markdown
   from `conversation.export()` and writes it to a file the user chooses in a native save dialog.

The code follows `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`. The renderer only uses `window.knowledgeBase`. File writing and the
save dialog run in the main process and are reached through new IPC channels exposed by the preload. The preload
bundle stays sandbox-safe. The docs (preload API, channel count and table, QuestionPanel) are updated.

## Markdown format

```
# Conversation export

## Question 1

<question text>

### Answer

<answer text>

### Citations

1. **<documentTitle>**
   > <excerpt line 1>
   > <excerpt line 2>

## Question 2
...
```

- Each history entry produces one `## Question N` section, with N starting at 1 and following history order.
  The question text appears in full, then `### Answer` and the full answer text.
- Every answer is followed by its citations, in the order stored on the answer. Each citation shows the
  document title and the excerpt. Every line of the excerpt is prefixed with `> `, so a multi-line excerpt
  stays inside its citation.
- When an answer has no citations, the `### Citations` heading is followed by the line `No citations.`
- When the conversation is empty, the document is `# Conversation export` followed by a line saying
  `No questions yet.`, with no `## Question` sections.
- Question, answer, title and excerpt text are copied as stored. This feature does not escape Markdown.

## Acceptance criteria

These are checked in the running app, using `window.knowledgeBase` and the UI over Chrome DevTools, with a
fresh `--user-data-dir` and `data/sample-documents/` imported and indexed.

1. `typeof window.knowledgeBase.conversation.export === 'function'`. The other preload namespaces (`documents`,
   `indexing`, `qa`, `feedback`, `app`) are unchanged.
2. With an empty history (a fresh profile, or after `qa.clearHistory()` or `app.reset()`), `export()` resolves
   to a string that contains `# Conversation export` and `No questions yet.` and does not contain
   `## Question`.
3. After asking 3 different questions (at least one answer has citations), `export()` contains exactly 3
   `## Question N` headings (1, 2, 3). Each heading is followed by that question's exact text, in the order
   the questions were asked, matching `qa.history()` order.
4. For each history entry, the answer text `response.answer` appears after its question and before the next
   `## Question` heading.
5. For each citation of each answer, the citation's `documentTitle` and every line of its `excerpt` (with the
   `> ` prefix) appear inside that answer's section, after the answer text, in the order the citations are
   stored. An answer without citations shows `No citations.` in its section.
6. `export()` reflects the current state: asking another question adds `## Question 4`, and after
   `qa.clearHistory()` the result is the empty document from criterion 2. Calling `export()` does not change
   `qa.history()`.
7. The question panel (the `<form>` that holds the "Ask a question" input) contains a `<button>` with
   `aria-label="Export conversation"`. Its `type` is not `submit`, so clicking it does not ask a question. It
   is shown and enabled both when the conversation is empty and when it is not.
8. Clicking the button opens a save dialog with a `.md` default file name. When the user picks a path, the file
   at that path contains exactly the string `conversation.export()` returns at that moment, in UTF-8. When the
   user cancels, no file is written and no error is shown.
   - **Testability:** a native dialog cannot be driven over CDP. When the environment variable
     `KB_EXPORT_SAVE_PATH` is set, the main process skips the dialog and uses that path as the chosen file,
     and the special value `cancel` simulates a cancelled dialog. Without the variable, the real dialog is
     used.
9. After a successful save, the UI shows a visible confirmation that includes the saved file path, for example
   `role="status"` text like `Conversation exported to <path>`. If writing fails (for example an unwritable
   or nonexistent directory), the UI shows a visible error message (`role="alert"`) and the app keeps working.
   A later question can still be asked.
10. The export (bridge and file) survives a restart: after the app is relaunched with the same
    `--user-data-dir`, `export()` returns the same questions, answers and citations.
11. Static and runtime checks pass: `npm run check`, `npm test` (with new tests for the Markdown builder,
    covering the empty case, ordering, citations and multi-line excerpts, plus the IPC/preload wiring and the
    button), `bash scripts/check-architecture.sh` and `bash scripts/smoke-bridge.sh`, which must list the
    `conversation` key.

## Out of scope

- Other formats (PDF, HTML, JSON) and import of an exported file.
- Including feedback ratings, confidence, timestamps or document ids in the export. These may be added only if
  they do not break the criteria above, and they are not required.
- Escaping Markdown special characters in user or document text.
- Exporting a subset of the conversation, or a single answer.
- Changes to Q&A, retrieval, citation quality, or the conversation history view.
- An export button outside the question panel.

# spec.md: export the conversation as Markdown

## Scope

"The conversation" is the persisted Q&A history: what `window.knowledgeBase.qa.history()` returns, in that order

1. **Bridge:** `window.knowledgeBase.conversation.export()` returns `Promise<string>`, a Markdown document built
   from the current history. It reads the history every time it runs and changes no data.
2. **UI:** the question panel gets a button with `aria-label="Export conversation"`. Clicking it gets the Markdown
   from `conversation.export()` and writes it to a file the user chooses in a native save dialog.

The code follows `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`. The renderer only uses `window.knowledgeBase`. File writing and the
save dialog run in the main process and are reached through new IPC channels exposed by the preload. The preload
bundle stays sandbox-safe. The docs (preload API, channel count and table, QuestionPanel) are updated.

## Markdown format

```
# Conversation export

## Question 1

<question text>

### Answer

<answer text>

### Citations

1. **<documentTitle>**
   > <excerpt line 1>
   > <excerpt line 2>

## Question 2
...
```

  The question text appears in full, then `### Answer` and the full answer text.

  document title and the excerpt. Every line of the excerpt is prefixed with `> `, so a multi-line excerpt
  stays inside its citation.

  `No questions yet.`, with no `## Question` sections.
